sentences.quote:
Brazil's Vivo fills CFO gap as Melcon heads for exit
2026-03-27T18:20:00Z
Telefonica|Vivo names Rodrigo Rossi Monari as new CFO, after current finance chief David Melcon heads to the UK's Virgin Media O2.
sentences.text: Chief Financial and Investor Relations Officer David Melcon Sanchez-Friera stepped down on April 2, 2026 to become CFO of VMED O2 UK, with the board set to choose his successor that same day; Rodrigo Monari has since served as CFO and Investor Relations Officer, alongside CEO Christian Mauad Gebara, whose mandate has been renewed through 2028.
Gebara also noted that after a new board member was appointed in April, women represent 42% of the board.

sentences.quote: Think Vivo strategy stands on upselling data, digital services, and totalization of customers.
sentences.text: On strategy, he stresses execution of a "more for more" approach based on upselling data, digital services and customer totalization, and is leaning on AI, including a customer-support revamp, to limit inflation's margin impact.

sentences.quote: Mobile ARPU of Telefonica Brasil increased to R$53.9, up 0.8 percent.
sentences.text: Vivo's mobile franchise keeps compounding: postpaid accesses reached 73.2 million in Q2 2026, up 6.9 percent, with postpaid net additions up 14.1 percent year over year, and mobile ARPU hit a record BRL 32.5 with postpaid churn at 1 percent.

sentences.quote: the company's fiber network expanded to 32.0 million homes passed, an increase of 6.4 percent. Connected fiber customers reached 8.2 million, growing 11.3 percent, lifting fiber take-up to 25.6 percent.
sentences.text: Fiber remains underpenetrated: the network reached 32.0 million homes passed and 8.2 million connected customers, a take-up of 25.6 percent, with broadband churn improving to 1.4 percent.

sentences.quote: digital B2B revenue expanded 14.9 percent over the last twelve months. New businesses, including electronics, health, streaming and financial services, recorded 33.6 percent revenue growth
sentences.text: Convergence and digital services add upside, as new-business revenue climbed 33.6 percent and digital B2B revenue rose 14.9 percent.
Profitability is improving, with Q2 2026 EBITDA of R$6.58 billion, up 10.9 percent, at a 41.8 percent margin.
Returns are backed by a light balance sheet: Telefonica Brasil distributed BRL 7 billion and targets at least 100 percent of 2026 net income, with net debt to EBITDA of 0.4x.
